t: Use Your Existing Phone Number for Outbound Calls with Verified Caller ID
html:
Voice calling in Eleva is now easier to try because users can place calls using a phone number they already own. This removes the need to purchase a Eleva number before testing outbound voice calling. Businesses can start calling leads and customers faster while deciding whether they need a full Eleva phone number setup later.

What is Calling With Your Existing Phone Number ?


Calling with your existing phone number allows users to place outbound voice calls from Eleva without first purchasing a Eleva phone number. This helps new users, agencies, and locations test voice calling with less setup effort and lower upfront commitment.


With this update, users can use a phone number they already own to make calls directly from Eleva. This is useful for businesses that want to try voice calling before setting up a dedicated Eleva number, porting an existing number, or configuring a full phone system.

Key Benefits of Calling With Your Existing Phone Number


Using an existing number helps teams start voice conversations faster. It reduces setup friction and gives users a simple way to experience outbound calling before making a longer-term phone system decision.

  • Lower Upfront Setup: Users can try voice calling without purchasing a Eleva number first.

  • Faster Testing: New locations can make calls sooner using a phone number they already own.

  • Easier Adoption: Agencies can help clients experience voice calling without requiring number purchase as the first step.

  • Flexible Phone Setup: Users can test outbound calling first and decide later whether to purchase, port, or configure a Eleva-managed number.

  • Improved Access to Calling: Locations without a Eleva phone number can still explore voice calling inside Eleva.

When to Use an Existing Phone Number for Voice Calls


Using an existing number is best for users who want to quickly try outbound voice calling in Eleva. This option is especially helpful when a business already has a trusted phone number and wants to start calling contacts before completing a full phone setup.


Use this option when:

  • You want to try voice calling before purchasing a Eleva number.

  • Your location does not currently have a phone number in Eleva.

  • You already own a business phone number you want to use for outbound calls.

  • You want a low-effort way to test calling workflows with leads or customers.

  • You are helping a client evaluate Eleva voice calling before completing phone number setup.


This option is not the same as porting a number into Eleva. Porting or purchasing a Eleva number may still be needed for full phone system functionality, depending on the use case.

Existing Number vs. Eleva Number


Understanding the difference between using an existing number and purchasing a Eleva number helps users choose the right setup. An existing number is useful for trying outbound calling, while a Eleva-managed number may be needed for more complete phone system configuration.

OptionBest ForNotes
Existing owned numberTrying outbound voice calling quicklyDoes not require purchasing a Eleva number first
Eleva phone numberFull phone setup inside ElevaUseful for managed calling, SMS, routing, and phone number configuration
Ported numberMoving an existing business number into ElevaUseful when the business wants Eleva to manage the number directly


The existing Knowledge Base includes verified caller ID setup for using your number for voice calls, outbound calling through the web dialer, and Eleva Phone billing details. These articles may be helpful when configuring or expanding calling functionality.

Important Limitations and Expectations


This feature is designed to reduce the barrier to trying voice calling. Setting expectations helps users understand what this option does and does not replace before they begin calling from Eleva.


1. Purchasing a Eleva number is no longer required before placing voice calls.

2. Support for placing voice calls using a phone number the user already owns.

3. Usage charges may still apply for voice calling. Review Eleva Phone billing details for current voice call pricing and related costs. 

4. Using an existing number for outbound calling is different from porting the number into Eleva.

5. Users who need full phone system functionality may still need to purchase, port, or configure a Eleva-managed number.


How To Setup Calling With Your Existing Phone Number


Proper setup ensures Eleva can recognize the phone number you want to use and allows you to start outbound calling with fewer interruptions. Verifying or selecting the correct number also helps contacts recognize your business when you call.


Follow these steps to place a voice call using an existing phone number:

  1. Log in to Eleva and open the correct sub-account.

  2. Navigate to the Phone System available in the Settings where outbound calls are placed.


  3. Choose the option to use an existing phone number, if prompted.



  4. Enter or select the phone number you already own.

  5. Complete verification steps shown in Eleva.




    • If a verification call is required, answer the call and enter the provided verification code.

    • The existing verified caller ID flow in Eleva uses a verification call and code to confirm ownership of the number.

  6. Open the Eleva dialer.

  7. Select the existing number as the calling number, if a “Calling From” or caller ID dropdown is shown.

  8. Enter the contact’s phone number or choose a contact from Eleva.

  9. Place the call.



Billing Considerations for Voice Calls


Voice calling may still have usage-based costs even when a Eleva phone number is not purchased first. Understanding billing helps users avoid confusion between phone number purchase costs and call usage charges.


The main cost difference is that users do not need to purchase a Eleva number upfront to try voice calling with an existing number. However, outbound voice usage may still be billed based on the applicable Eleva Phone rates.


Review the Eleva Phone Pricing & Billing Guide for current phone number costs, voice call rates, messaging rates, carrier fees, and rebilling information.

Note- Countries Where Verified Caller ID Is Not Supported for Local Calls


Calls using a Verified Caller ID  are not supported for domestic calls in the some countries due to local regulations and/or carrier restrictions like

  • India
  • Malaysia
  • Finland
  • Thailand
  • Taiwan
  • Greece etc

In these countries, calls placed using a Verified Caller ID may be blocked or may not complete reliably. In such cases to ensure successful call delivery, use either a local phone number for the destination country (where supported) or an international phone number to place the call.

Frequently Asked Questions


Q: Do I need to buy a Eleva number before making voice calls?
A: No. Eleva allows users to place voice calls using a phone number they already own, so purchasing a Eleva number first is no longer required.


Q: Can I use any phone number I own?
A: Eleva confirms that users can place calls using a phone number they already own. Use the phone number options shown in Eleva to confirm whether your specific number can be added or verified.


Q: Is this the same as verified caller ID?
A: It may use a similar ownership verification concept, but Eleva does not explicitly confirm that it is the same flow. Eleva’s existing verified caller ID article explains how users verify their own phone number for voice calls.


Q: Can I receive inbound calls in Eleva using my existing number?
A: Eleva only confirms placing voice calls. It does not confirm inbound calling support for existing owned numbers. Users who need inbound call routing may need a Eleva-managed number, forwarding setup, or number porting, depending on their phone setup.


Q: Can I send SMS from my existing number?
A: Eleva only mentions voice calling. It does not confirm SMS support using an existing owned number.


Q: Will I still be charged for calls?
A: Purchasing a Eleva number first is no longer required, but voice usage charges may still apply. Review Eleva Phone billing details for current call pricing.


Q: Is using my existing number the same as porting it into Eleva?
A: No. Using an existing number for voice calls allows you to place calls with that number. Porting moves number management into Eleva.


Q: Can I purchase or port a number later?
A: Yes. Using an existing number to try calling does not prevent users from purchasing a Eleva number or porting a number later if they need a fuller phone setup.


Q: Is this the same as Verified Caller ID?
A: Yes. Your existing phone number is verified and added as a Verified Caller ID, allowing it to appear as the caller ID for outbound calls placed through Eleva.
